findings.issue_text: `downsize` is defined twice in app/models/optimized_image.rb (4-arg and 3-arg versions); Ruby's last-definition-wins silently replaces the first, making the documented 4-arg API dead code — callers using `OptimizedImage.downsize(src, dst, 1024, 768)` bind max_height into opts, and `optimize` then raises TypeError when `opts[:allow_animation]` is called on an Integer

`optimize`'s arity changed from 6 params to 5, so any other wrapper in optimized_image.rb still calling `optimize(op, from, to, w, h, opts)` (e.g. a crop wrapper) will now raise ArgumentError (6 for 4..5) — all optimize call sites need verifying

Animated-GIF downsize path is unreachable for the new controller call: `optimize` selects `downsize_instructions_animated` only when the `from` path matches /\.GIF$/i, but tempfile paths (Rack multipart and FileHelper.download) have no extension, so animated GIFs are downsized with single-frame instructions (no -coalesce), resizing delta frames independently and producing broken/corrupted animations; the check should key off the original filename/content type

Hardcoded `10.megabytes` download cap in uploads_controller.rb ignores `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so admins who raised the setting above 10240 now have previously-valid 10–20 MB URL-based uploads abort (FileHelper.download returns nil via rescue nil); the nil tempfile then flows into `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` causing NoMethodError → 500

Client-side size check in utilities.js is hardcoded to 10 MB for every upload type, discarding `max_#{type}_size_kb`: (a) if max_attachment_size_kb < 10240, oversized attachments are no longer blocked client-side and may be accepted end-to-end if the web server's client_max_body_size is ≥ 10 MB; (b) admins who raise max_image_size_kb above 10 MB still get client-side rejection of raw files > 10 MB; the limit should be derived from the setting

413 handler in utilities.js reports a hardcoded '10240 KB' limit, but 413 comes from the web server's independently configured client_max_body_size, so users hitting the real limit are told a wrong maximum

Downsize failures are swallowed in uploads_controller.rb: the loop ignores `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s false return value, retries a failing conversion 5× on the unchanged file, never verifies the target size was reached (5 × 80% may be insufficient for extreme ratios), and a partially-written/truncated tempfile from a failed convert can flow into `Upload.create_for`; the return value should be checked with a log/bail on failure

Synchronous multi-pass ImageMagick downsize loop (up to 5 iterations) runs inline in the controller request thread, pinning puma workers for seconds per upload and causing thread-pool exhaustion and site-wide latency degradation under concurrent uploads, instead of following Discourse's established pattern of pushing image work to background jobs

The convert subprocess is executed via a blocking backtick call with no timeout, so a degenerate image (decompression bomb under 10MB compressed but enormous in raw pixels) can make a single convert run for minutes, multiplied up to 5x by the retry loop

Per-request download cap changed from the site-configured SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb to a hardcoded 10.megabytes, decoupling this cost driver from admin config so the full 10MB is fetched and CPU-processed before any size decision instead of being rejected at the download boundary

Animated GIFs always take the expensive generic convert path because the _animated instruction branch requires from =~ /\.GIF$/i but from is always an extension-less tempfile path (RackMultipart.../Tempfile.new), making the animation-aware path dead code; multi-frame GIF decode cost scales with frames x pixels and can expand a 10MB GIF to hundreds of MB or spill to ImageMagick's disk-backed pixel cache, repeated up to 5 times inline in the request

The downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's false return value, blindly re-spawning the identical failing convert command until attempts are exhausted (5 wasted process spawns) and then proceeding with Upload.create_for on the unchanged over-limit file, silently defeating the size cap

Client-side size gate in utilities.js hardcoded to 10 * 1024 instead of derived from Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so uploads the server policy would reject are fully transferred before failing (wasted bandwidth/latency) and the 413 error message always reports 10240 regardless of the real configured limit

Hardcoded 10MB client cap in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 replaces per-type site settings for ALL upload types: attachments between the admin-configured limit and 10MB now pass client validation and get sent/stored (server-side path has no size check for non-images), silently bypassing the admin's attachment limit; files above 10MB that the site explicitly allows are rejected client-side with 'file too large (10240 KB)'

Animated GIF detection can never match: OptimizedImage.optimize selects downsize_instructions_animated only when from =~ /\.GIF$/i, but from is a Rack multipart tempfile path (e.g. RackMultipart20150612-3-1h6vq9j) with no extension, so animated GIFs are downsized with non-animated instructions (no -coalesce), resizing each delta frame independently and producing a broken/flattened animation — permanently, since the original tempfile is rewritten in place, even when allow_animated_thumbnails is true

Retry loop in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-68 ignores the downsize result and has no progress/failure check: OptimizedImage.downsize returns falsey when convert fails but the return value is discarded, so on persistent failure the loop blindly re-runs the same failing conversion 5 times; because from == to (in-place rewrite), a convert that fails partway (e.g. disk full) can leave the tempfile truncated/corrupted, and that corrupted file is then uploaded as the user's content

After 5 attempts the still-oversized file is uploaded anyway in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-70: the loop exits after attempt reaches 0 regardless of size and Upload.create_for proceeds unconditionally; five passes at 80% only guarantees ~10x area reduction (0.8^5), so images that don't shrink enough (e.g. small-dimension/large-file PNGs) are stored exceeding max_image_size_kb with no error to anyone

Hardcoded 10MB download cap in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 regresses API URL uploads: the cap was SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes and is now 10.megabytes, so on sites that raised max_image_size_kb above 10MB, API-supplied URLs pointing at 10MB–limit images now exceed the download cap; FileHelper.download raises, rescue nil yields tempfile = nil, and Upload.create_for calls nil.size → NoMethodError → 500 (the nil-tempfile crash is pre-existing but this change newly triggers it for uploads that previously succeeded)

413 error message in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 hardcodes 10MB: the 'file_too_large' message shown after a 413 from the web server now always reports 10240 KB regardless of the actual configured max_image_size_kb / nginx client_max_body_size, so users get a wrong limit in the error dialog whenever settings differ from 10MB

No timeout around synchronous ImageMagick conversion in the request thread in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67: up to 5 sequential convert invocations run inline in the web request via backticks with no timeout, so a pathological image (a ≤10MB compressed decompression bomb is feasible) can pin a Puma worker for the duration of 5 conversions with no bound, degrading availability; there is no circuit-breaker or fallback if convert hangs

Downsizing is skipped entirely when the filename has no image extension in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64: FileHelper.is_image?(filename) is extension-based, and for the API URL path filename = File.basename(URI.parse(url).path), so extension-less image URLs (S3 signed URLs, CDN routes, etc.) skip the downsize branch completely and an image up to the 10MB download cap is stored as-is even though it exceeds max_image_size_kb — pre-PR these were at least capped at the setting, now the limit is bypassed

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `OptimizedImage.optimize` from taking separate `width, height` to a single `dimensions` string (`def self.optimize(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts={})`). The shown call sites for `resize` were updated accordingly, but the finding’s concern is that any other callers (e.g. other wrappers in the same file) might still be passing `w, h` as separate args and would then raise `ArgumentError`. The diff itself doesn’t show any such remaining call sites, so this is a verification/sweep concern rather than a defect proven by the shown hunks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Animated-GIF downsize path is unreachable for the new controller call: `optimize` selects `downsize_instructions_animated` only when the `from` path matches /\.GIF$/i, but tempfile paths (Rack multipart and FileHelper.download) have no extension, so animated GIFs are downsized with single-frame instructions (no -coalesce), resizing delta frames independently and producing broken/corrupted animations; the check should key off the original filename/content type

adjudication.rationale: The new controller logic calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` where `from` is the tempfile path. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, animated handling is selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true and `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. If the tempfile path lacks a `.gif` extension (common for `Tempfile`/downloads), `downsize_instructions_animated` won’t be used even for animated GIF uploads, so animation-safe processing (e.g., coalesce) would be skipped. This is a correctness risk introduced/exposed by the new downsize-on-upload path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded `10.megabytes` download cap in uploads_controller.rb ignores `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so admins who raised the setting above 10240 now have previously-valid 10–20 MB URL-based uploads abort (FileHelper.download returns nil via rescue nil); the nil tempfile then flows into `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` causing NoMethodError → 500

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, URL-based uploads now call `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) rescue nil` instead of using `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. If the URL download fails/raises (e.g., because the remote file exceeds 10MB), `tempfile` becomes `nil` due to `rescue nil`. The new downsizing guard checks `if tempfile && ...`, but immediately after the code unconditionally does `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)`, which will raise `NoMethodError` when `tempfile` is nil, causing a 500. This is directly introduced by the hardcoded cap + `rescue nil` + unconditional `tempfile.size` usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side size check in utilities.js is hardcoded to 10 MB for every upload type, discarding `max_#{type}_size_kb`: (a) if max_attachment_size_kb < 10240, oversized attachments are no longer blocked client-side and may be accepted end-to-end if the web server's client_max_body_size is ≥ 10 MB; (b) admins who raise max_image_size_kb above 10 MB still get client-side rejection of raw files > 10 MB; the limit should be derived from the setting

413 handler in utilities.js reports a hardcoded '10240 KB' limit, but 413 comes from the web server's independently configured client_max_body_size, so users hitting the real limit are told a wrong maximum

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the 413 case now hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` (10MB) instead of using a setting (`Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`). That means the user-facing “file too large” message for HTTP 413 is no longer tied to any actual configured limit and can easily become misleading if the real upload limit differs. The diff does show the hardcoding; it does not show the server’s actual 413 limit configuration, so the mismatch is a plausible consistency/UX issue rather than a definitively verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize failures are swallowed in uploads_controller.rb: the loop ignores `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s false return value, retries a failing conversion 5× on the unchanged file, never verifies the target size was reached (5 × 80% may be insufficient for extreme ratios), and a partially-written/truncated tempfile from a failed convert can flow into `Upload.create_for`; the return value should be checked with a log/bail on failure

adjudication.rationale: The new upload resizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` but ignores its (falsey) return value and always decrements `attempt`. If the conversion fails, nothing in the loop logs/bails, and the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` with the same tempfile path. Since the output overwrites the input (`from` == `to`), a failed/partial convert could leave a bad tempfile that still gets uploaded. The loop also does not explicitly validate that the final size is within `max_image_size_kb` before continuing (it only stops retrying after 5 attempts).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Synchronous multi-pass ImageMagick downsize loop (up to 5 iterations) runs inline in the controller request thread, pinning puma workers for seconds per upload and causing thread-pool exhaustion and site-wide latency degradation under concurrent uploads, instead of following Discourse's established pattern of pushing image work to background jobs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds synchronous, potentially multi-iteration ImageMagick work directly in `UploadsController#create_upload`: a `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` loop calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times before `Upload.create_for(...)`. `OptimizedImage.convert_with` executes shell commands via backticks synchronously, so this processing runs inline on the request thread and can tie up Puma workers during uploads under concurrency. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by the change, not a functional correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The convert subprocess is executed via a blocking backtick call with no timeout, so a degenerate image (decompression bomb under 10MB compressed but enormous in raw pixels) can make a single convert run for minutes, multiplied up to 5x by the retry loop

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a retry loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that can invoke `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times while the tempfile remains larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. `OptimizedImage.convert_with` executes the ImageMagick command via a blocking backtick call (`` `#{instructions.join(" ")} &> /dev/null` ``) with no timeout/kill mechanism. This makes the upload request potentially block for an unbounded time per attempt, now multiplied by the new loop, creating a plausible DoS/performance/security defect grounded in the added loop and existing blocking subprocess call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-request download cap changed from the site-configured SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb to a hardcoded 10.megabytes, decoupling this cost driver from admin config so the full 10MB is fetched and CPU-processed before any size decision instead of being rejected at the download boundary

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the API URL download limit in `UploadsController#create_upload` from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). The new downsize loop only runs after the tempfile has been fully downloaded, so the site setting no longer constrains the per-request network/download cost at the boundary; it only constrains post-download resizing. This is a real, diff-grounded architectural/resource-control concern, but it’s not unambiguously a correctness defect since the behavior may be intentional (allow oversize images to be reduced).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Animated GIFs always take the expensive generic convert path because the _animated instruction branch requires from =~ /\.GIF$/i but from is always an extension-less tempfile path (RackMultipart.../Tempfile.new), making the animation-aware path dead code; multi-frame GIF decode cost scales with frames x pixels and can expand a 10MB GIF to hundreds of MB or spill to ImageMagick's disk-backed pixel cache, repeated up to 5 times inline in the request

adjudication.rationale: In the new upload downsizing loop, the code calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` (uploads_controller.rb). In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated branch is selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true *and* `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Here `from` is `tempfile.path`, which is typically a Rack/Ruby Tempfile path without a `.gif` suffix, so even for an animated GIF upload the `_animated` instruction path likely won’t be taken. This defeats the intent of passing `allow_animation:` and can lead to incorrect handling of animated GIFs during the up-to-5 retry downsizing loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's false return value, blindly re-spawning the identical failing convert command until attempts are exhausted (5 wasted process spawns) and then proceeding with Upload.create_for on the unchanged over-limit file, silently defeating the size cap

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb` a new loop repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` while the tempfile is still over `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, but it never checks whether the downsize operation succeeded. The diff shows `OptimizedImage.convert_with` returns `false` when the underlying convert command fails (`return false if $?.exitstatus != 0`), so a failing convert will leave `tempfile.size` unchanged, causing up to 5 identical failing process spawns and then continuing to `Upload.create_for(...)` without any explicit handling of the failure/oversize condition.

The finding’s additional claim about server-side size enforcement/bypass for non-images cannot be verified from this diff alone, but the client-side regression is real and introduced here.

adjudication.rationale: The new upload logic downsizes images in place via `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` (uploads_controller.rb). In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, animated handling is only selected when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true *and* `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` (optimized_image.rb). Here `from` is the tempfile path (e.g., RackMultipart... in /tmp) which typically has no `.gif` extension, so `downsize_instructions_animated` will not be used even for GIF uploads. Because the downsizing rewrites `tempfile.path` in place before creating the `Upload`, this would permanently process animated GIFs with the non-animated pipeline.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb a new retry loop downsizes the same tempfile in-place: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` inside a `while attempt > 0 ...` loop. The return value from `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored, and in optimized_image.rb the pipeline ultimately returns `false` on conversion failure (`convert_with` returns false when `$?.exitstatus != 0`). With no check for failure/progress, a persistent conversion failure will simply rerun up to 5 times and then proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` with whatever state the tempfile is left in. Because the conversion is in-place (from == to), a failed/partial write can plausibly leave the tempfile corrupted/truncated with no guard in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop downsizes at most 5 times (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`) and then always proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` without any explicit check or user-facing error if the file is still above `max_image_size_kb`. The finding’s core point (no post-loop enforcement/feedback) is verifiable from the diff. However, whether an oversized image would actually be stored depends on validations inside `Upload.create_for` (not shown in the diff), so the “stored exceeding max_image_size_kb” claim can’t be confirmed here.

The nil-tempfile crash path exists in this method and this change makes it newly reachable for uploads that previously succeeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsizing is skipped entirely when the filename has no image extension in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64: FileHelper.is_image?(filename) is extension-based, and for the API URL path filename = File.basename(URI.parse(url).path), so extension-less image URLs (S3 signed URLs, CDN routes, etc.) skip the downsize branch completely and an image up to the 10MB download cap is stored as-is even though it exceeds max_image_size_kb — pre-PR these were at least capped at the setting, now the limit is bypassed

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing logic in `uploads_controller.rb` only runs when `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is true. For API URL uploads, `filename = File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)` can be extension-less (common for signed/CDN URLs), making `is_image?` likely return false (extension-based as the finding notes). Since the download cap was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to `10.megabytes`, those extension-less image URLs can now be downloaded up to 10MB and will skip the newly added downsizing loop intended to bring images back under `max_image_size_kb`, creating a regression relative to the prior setting-based cap.
